name: Himlung Himal Expedition
region: Annapurna / Manang (Nar-Phu, Peri Himal); often grouped with the Manaslu area
sub_region: Narpa Bhumi Rural Municipality-5, Manang District, Gandaki Province (Nepal-Tibet border)

difficulty.notes: Glaciated 7,000 m peak climbed with fixed ropes, crampons and three high camps; marketed as a step-up peak for climbers with 6,000 m experience. No formal alpine grade found in authoritative sources. [s5, s6, s9]

duration_days.notes: Operators list 24-35 days: approx. 7-9 days approach via Besisahar/Koto and the Nar-Phu valley, approx. 10-14 days of rotations and summit window above base camp, then 2-3 days return. [s5, s6, s7]

itinerary.route: Arrival in Kathmandu; gear check, permits and briefing
Drive Kathmandu - Besisahar - Koto (Annapurna Circuit road)
Trek Koto - Nar Khola gorge - Meta - Chyaku/Kyang - Phu Gaon
itinerary.notes: Enters the Nar-Phu restricted area at Koto. Phu Gaon altitude given as 4,080-4,250 m. [s5, s7]

itinerary.route: Puja, training, and acclimatization rotations to Camp I (approx. 5,400-5,500 m), Camp II (approx. 6,000 m) and Camp III (approx. 6,350-6,400 m); summit push in a weather window
itinerary.walking_hours: Summit day approx. 6-8 hours up from high camp
itinerary.notes: Camp altitudes vary by operator and season. [s5, s6, s7]

itinerary.route: Descend to Phu, trek out via Meta/Koto, drive to Besisahar and Kathmandu
itinerary.notes: Some operators drive from Dharapani. [s7, s8]

best_seasons.notes: Autumn is the main commercial season. On 27 Sep 2026 (some reports say 26 Sep) an avalanche buried Himlung Base Camp after heavy snowfall, killing 15 Nepali workers with one missing; no foreign climbers were on the mountain yet. [s7, s10, s11, s12]

permits.name: Department of Tourism climbing royalty (7,001-7,500 m category)
permits.fee: Foreign climber per person: USD 800 spring, USD 400 autumn, USD 200 winter/summer

permits.name: Garbage management deposit (refundable, per expedition team)
permits.fee: USD 500 if classed outside the Khumbu/Annapurna ranges, or USD 2,000 if classed in the 7,001-8,000 m Khumbu/Annapurna category - classification for Himlung not confirmed

permits.name: Nar-Phu Restricted Area Permit (Narpa Bhumi RM wards 1-5, Nasho RM wards 6-7)
permits.fee: Sep-Nov: USD 100 per person per week + USD 15/day beyond; Dec-Aug: USD 75 per week + USD 15/day beyond. Department of Immigration states climbers holding an expedition permit must still obtain the trekking permit for restricted areas but do not pay its fee.

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP)
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person per entry (SAARC NPR 1,000)

permits.name: Government liaison officer
permits.fee: Required/arranged by operators; official fee not found

guide_requirements: Under the sixth amendment of Nepal's Mountaineering Regulation (in force 1 Sept 2025), teams climbing peaks other than 8,000 m peaks must take at least one mountain guide. Nar-Phu is a restricted area: permit via a registered agency with a licensed guide. Mandatory accident insurance minimums apply to guides, high-altitude workers, liaison officers and base camp staff. [s2, s4, s14, s15]

drives: Besisahar - Koto by jeep on the Annapurna Circuit road (some itineraries continue to/from Dharapani)
logistics.notes: Teahouses/lodges on the approach to Phu; tented base camp and high camps. [s5, s7, s9]

highlights: 7,126 m summit on the Nepal-Tibet border
Approach through the Nar-Phu valley and the medieval village of Phu
Popular preparation peak before 8,000 m expeditions
risks: Avalanche: Sept 2026 base camp avalanche killed 15 Nepali staff
High altitude above 7,000 m; frostbite and AMS/HAPE/HACE
Heavy autumn snowfall and weather delays

acclimatization.notes: Typically one rest day at Phu, two to three days at base camp, then rotations before the summit push. [s5, s7]

unverified: Garbage deposit for Himlung: USD 500 or USD 2,000 depending on whether DoT classes it under the Annapurna range.
Liaison officer fee/requirement details for Himlung were not found in official sources.
Phu Gaon altitude varies between 4,080 m and 4,250 m in operator sources; high camp altitudes vary by operator.
Date of the 2026 avalanche is reported as 26 Sep (Kathmandu Post) and 27 Sep (Himalayan Times, BBC).
